title: Invisible Users, Invisible Interfaces: Accelerating Design Iteration with AI Simulation - Alex Liss
talk_summary: A design-agency data scientist proposes using LLM 'intelligent twins' (persona simulations grounded in audience data) to run scripted task audits of websites, replacing slow human heuristic analysis with fast, scalable simulated user testing. The talk is mostly conceptual/marketing with one small sample project (72 simulated actions across 3 sports sites) and no measured quality or cost results.

takeaways.evidence_quote: with four tasks per category and that allows us to simulate 72 AI simulated actions
takeaways.numbers: 72 simulated actions; 2 personas; 3 websites; 4 tasks per category

takeaways.technique: Standardize simulation params in a repo
takeaways.what_they_do: They plan to put briefing instructions, audience dimensions, number of audit runs, and task-completion/failure thresholds into a versioned code repository so runs are reproducible and comparable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: standardizing things in a code repository that lays out parameters like the briefing instructions, the simulated audience dimensions, the number of audit runs

takeaways.what_they_do: They propose running the simulated method alongside human teams in a test/control design to isolate where simulation helps and where it doesn't, across domains.
takeaways.evidence_quote: applying it through a test and control methodology will also be useful to help us isolate what the strengths are

takeaways.technique: Briefed simulated agents as active design participants
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of static data artifacts, they turn audience data into 'intelligent twins' that are briefed with specific tasks and evaluate interfaces like a human doing heuristic analysis.
takeaways.evidence_quote: brief intelligent twins to evaluate interfaces by focusing on specific tasks much as we might brief a human designer to conduct a heristic analysis

takeaways.technique: High-level rollup plus drill-down from one simulation run
takeaways.what_they_do: The same simulated run is aggregated to category-level findings and also drilled into specific friction points, producing both broad and narrow design briefs from one dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the different levels of altitude this methodology can operate at allows us to create uh design briefs which are really focused which are really broad and really deep
